title: 1981-04-16_Pat_22.txt
concise_summary: PKD synthesizes Cartesian-Malebranchian epistemology with his own theory of consciousness to argue that God must actively compel our assent to reality, not merely present perceptions. Drawing on the separation of experience from assent he witnessed during his 2-74 visions and supported by hallucination phenomenology, he claims his entire corpus documents a lifelong cognitive blindness cured only when he achieved authentic being (Heidegger's sein) by confronting reality in primal Angst.
key_claims: We do not directly experience the world but only a representation of world that God compels us to assent to; perception and assent are separable acts
God's mediation must occur directly in/through the mind; the representation itself cannot compel assent, only God can
Hallucinations demonstrate that experiencing something and taking it as real are distinct cognitive processes, proving the problem of compelled assent is genuine and profound
PKD experienced cognitive rather than perceptual blindness his entire life, cured only in 2-74 when he shifted from flight (inauthentic existence) to facing reality (Heideggerian sein)
The difference between the fictional realities in his novels and actual reality is precisely that God is absent in his fiction and present in the actual world
What he perceived in 2-74 was not miraculous but the regular operations of the universe seen correctly for the first time by a percipient no longer in flight
recurring_concepts: The meta-novel framework (ten-volume project studying perception/assent)

tensions: How can PKD claim 2-74 was seeing 'correctly' while also claiming he was cognitively blind all his life? (Resolved: the blindness was cognitive/assent-based, not perceptual; 2-74 activated the assent mechanism itself)
If God always compels our assent to normal perception, why doesn't everyone experience what PKD did in 2-74? (Unresolved tension about universality of the mechanism vs. PKD's exceptional recovery)
PKD says the signal discrimination 'wore off' — does this mean his post-2-74 perception is now again deluded or mediated differently? (Acknowledged but not fully resolved)

Tension between occasionalism (God is sole cause) and perceiving 'regular operations of the universe' — is God's action the regular operation or supplementary? (PKD claims they're identical but distinction remains)
Is the 'two signal discrimination' failure (wearing off) evidence of readjustment/health or loss of grace? (Framed as psychological adjustment but theological valence ambiguous)
How does Heideggerian sein (secular phenomenology) fit into Christian theology without collapse into each? (Conceptually synthesized but tensions remain)

reading_excerpt: In 2-74 God palpably entered my field of perception, which means that, as I theorize in the Platt interview, for the first time in my life I became sane.
raw_text: the universe functions - but, then, what we know as "world" is not in fact "world" at all but a representation in our minds that God compels our assent to (this last is my contribution; God does not have to make the world real qua world, only real to us). folder 90 - 123 folder 90 - 123 G-68 What this all adds up to is that for which Kant is so noted: that we do not experience "world" but only a representation of world (+ I say each of us probably experience a somewhat different one). (+ I say, too, that God does not have to make world real but, rather, real to us, which means that -in my system- he compels our assent to the representation by his acting directly on -more precisely in- our minds; thus the representation does not directly impinge on us but rather the representation in + through God - a view that Malebranche would heartily approve of, for it goes back to Malebranche's own source, Paul's statement that "we see all in God.") I suppose this, then, is what my meta-abstraction was actually about: that I did not experience world but world-in-God, hence not world per se at all. I am -as all men are- totally dependent on God for any notion of things outside me. I do not see corporeal things nor am I even capable of existing except through, in + by God, + he is in truth in me so-to-speak as me - this is Malebranche's primary view / insight. What I myself perceive (comprehend) is that only God -God alone- can compel my assent to the representation of world (intelligible archetypal ideas) which he impresses on me. Without God, even if I would somehow in some way discern things outside myself (the reality field) it would not be convincing - + this precisely is the topic of my 10 volume meta novel, this problem (linked to plural subjective private folder 90 - 124 folder 90 - 124 G-69 worlds; in other words I would be totally encapsulated + soon go crazy; I would be imprisoned by myself, knowing only myself. God + the "other" then are one + the same. We take our knowledge of the "other" (objects / reality outside us) for granted which is naive; + I point out (this is particularly my contribution) that even if we could somehow discern creation on our own, say through our senses, it would fail to compel our assent; i.e. it would fail to convince as real. One clue to all this -to this as a problem + genuine issue- as Malebranche himself realized is the phenomenon of hallucinations. +, with it, to a lesser but still genuine degree, the distortions known to us as delusional perception - in contradistinction to pure hallucinations, my point being not quite Malebranche's: my point is, when a person hallucinates, he not only experiences -perceives, sees, hears, smells, etc- the hallucination but is ineluctably compelled to take it as real; viz: it is not merely ghostly, phantasmic, only semireal, like static - noise versus signal; he is compelled to take it as signal. This shows that the issue confronted here is profound + important + not either merely technical or frivolous. My 10 volume meta novel right up to "Frozen Journey" is one colossal study of this problem, with no solution given (because I had no solution! The solution I see now is the only possible one: that some absolute agency compels our assent to what we folder 90 - 125 folder 90 - 125 G-70 experience - first causes us to experience it + then compels our assent; I have thus broken the situation down into two parts, in what perhaps is a further analysis of the problem vis-a-vis Cartesian analysis. For example, while on psychotomimetic drugs one experiences delusions + hallucinations but is not necessary compelled to assent; this is a matter of staggering importance; it means that the experience of + assent to can be distinguished. So more than perceptual involvement is involved; the cognitive system of the mind, over + above the percept-system is engaged. Thus (I reason) God must be in us (were he not, only the percept-system at most would be engaged, we might experience -perceive- but retain the option of rejecting as irreal what we perceive; however this is not the case. Thus there is no way I can distinguish myself from God-in-me. Now, my 10 volume meta novel can be construed as (as I say) one vast titanic study of this, with an awareness built into it that perception + assent can be separated - just take "Frozen Journey" alone! First Victor Kemmings perceives the irreal + gives assent; later he perceives the real + with-holds assent! Thus it can correctly be said that my corpus of writing is one long search for God, + that in "Valis" I have found him - in two ways: in my mind + in reality. One could correctly say that Phil Dick writes about what it would be like without God. So my Q: "How does God relate to the universe, + if he did not exist folder 90 - 126 G-71 what difference if any would we notice?" I have already answered my own question in + by means of my total corpus of writing. The difference between the "realities" of my writings + the actual world is that God is absent in the realities of my writing + present in the world we actually know. Well, then in 2-74 God palpably entered my field of perception, which means that, as I theorize in the Platt interview, for the first time in my life I became sane. I became as other people are ordinarily. But I got the experience of him rushing into my experience of world, my percept- + cognitive-systems, from which in a certain sense he had been absent. Viewing world for the first time (hence I said, "I am no longer blind!") I could discern him, which people "sighted" from birth have lost the ability to do. In other words, my phosphene-activity trip was world bursting in on me for the first time, because up to then I had been in one vast flight from it, but, at last, through primal Angst, I turned about-face + looked at it. Which is why I have supposed Heidegger's inauthentic existence being replaced by sein. I truly saw, because I was no longer running (my "chain ... web" satori). This is indeed Heidegger's sein, ushered in -as he says- by absolute Angst. In view of the possibility / probability that each of us experiences a somewhat different reality or representation of reality? My 10 volume meta novel deals with this, of course, as I eternally point out. However (as I say supra) I now see the issue or problem -or in fact solution- this way: How are we able to assent to the representation? + I believe that only God is able to compel that assent, + this is essential - that he do this for us, since otherwise our experience will be with something unconvincing (I do not deem it within the power of the representation in itself to compel this assent, but since God always -or almost always- compels our assent we are unaware of the problem + presume unquestioningly that there is no problem, the representation seems self-authenticating.
